title: The Limey
events_chronological: Wilson, a career thief, spends nine years in an English prison while his daughter Jenny grows up without him.
Jenny goes to Los Angeles and takes up with the record producer Terry Valentine.
Jenny works out that Valentine is laundering drug money and threatens to go to the police.
Valentine's head of security kills Jenny and stages a car crash on a canyon road.
Wilson is released, reads a newspaper cutting somebody has posted to him, and flies out.
Wilson finds Ed Roel, an acquaintance of Jenny's, who tells him what little he knows.
Wilson goes to a warehouse to ask questions, is beaten and thrown into the street, and walks back in and kills everyone in it.
Wilson meets Elaine, Jenny's acting teacher, who tells him exactly what sort of father he was.
Wilson and Roel watch Valentine's house from the hills above it.
Wilson crashes a party at the house, and the security men drive him into the desert to shoot him.
Wilson kills the men in the desert and walks back out to the road.
Valentine runs to a beach house up the coast with his young girlfriend.
Wilson and Roel drive north, and Roel is shot dead in the assault on the beach house.
Wilson corners Valentine on the rocks, and Valentine admits the girl's death came out of his own panic.
Wilson lets Valentine live, flies home, and thinks about a day at the seaside with Jenny as a small child.
syuzhet_notes: The film cuts a single conversation across three different places and times at once, and drops shots of the flight home into scenes that precede it. The result has no stable present: the same exchange belongs to several moments.
fabula_notes: The chronology is recoverable from the plot mechanics - the release, the flight, the deaths - even though almost no shot sits cleanly inside one moment.
